subject: language_arts

unit.title: Spelling with suffixes
unit.essentialQuestion: How do I add an ending to a word so it's still spelled correctly?

topic: Adding suffixes with no spelling change
title: Just add it on: -ing, -ed, -er, -est
objectives: By the end, I can add a suffix to a word that needs no spelling change.

vocabulary.definition: the main word before any ending
vocabulary.example: jump is the root of jumping

vocabulary.definition: a little ending (tail) added to a word

emphasize: A suffix is a tail you add to a root word to change it. Today's rule is the easy one: just add it on — NO spelling change.
Keep the root word visible and unchanged so the child sees nothing inside it changes — this builds the habit before the trickier rules (drop-e, double, y→i) in Lessons 6–8.
Repeated image: 'Grow a tail onto the root.' Pre-empt over-thinking (changing the root, e.g. plaing) and tail mix-ups (-ing vs -ed).

keyConcepts: for these roots, the suffix attaches with no spelling change
misconceptions: mixing up which tail was asked for (-ing vs -ed)
not reading the new word back after building it
hooks: Jump grows a tail and becomes jumping — grow tails on words!
priorKnowledge: what a root word is; adding -s to make a plural (Year 1)

digital: root-word cards on screen (jump, play, help, paint, kick, fast)
suffix tail cards (-ing, -ed, -er, -est) that slide onto the roots
whiteboard showing root + tail in two colours

video.searchTerm: adding the suffixes -ing and -ed to root words year 2
video.watchTask: Every time a suffix is added, say the root word and the tail OUT LOUD before the video joins them.

afterCheck.question: What do we call the little ending we add to a root word?

plan.goal: Introduce root + suffix with the 'grow a tail' image on jump → jumping; retrieve Year 1 plural -s.
plan.note: The tail card visibly slides onto the root on screen. Keep the two words root/suffix light — the image does the work.
plan.successCriteria: Child answers that cat becomes cats by adding -s, and is keen to grow tails.

script.say: I've got a word: jump. Watch — I'm going to grow a little tail on the end of it. Jump… plus -ing… becomes JUMPING! That little tail is called a suffix, and the main word, jump, is the root. You already know a tiny tail — how do I make cat into more than one cat?
script.adaptHints: If the child likes animals, play with the tail image — a word growing a tail like a puppy. If plural -s is shaky: 'One cat… two… cats — we added an s. Endings change words. Today's ending is a bigger one called a suffix.'

stuckProtocol: If plural -s is shaky: 'One cat… two… cats — we added an s. Endings change words. Today's ending is a bigger one called a suffix.'

plan.goal: Teach the easy rule: just stick the suffix straight on — nothing inside the root changes. Model jump/play with -ing and -ed.
plan.note: Write the root, then the suffix in a different colour, so the unchanged root stays clearly visible every time.
plan.successCriteria: Child can say 'the root doesn't change — just add the tail'.

script.say: The main word is the ROOT. The ending we add is the SUFFIX. For today's easy words, I just stick the suffix straight on — nothing inside the root changes. Watch: jump + -ing = jumping. Jump + -ed = jumped. See? The jump stays exactly the same, I just grow the tail. Let's try play: play + -ing = playing; play + -ed = played. Easy — just add it on. The root word doesn't change at all.
script.adaptHints: Point at the root each time: 'still spelled j-u-m-p — nothing changed.' Say the rule phrase twice: 'just add it on.'

blocks.caption: The root never changes — just add the tail!

blocks.definition: a little ending (tail) added to a root word

plan.goal: Shared building: help → helping/helped, paint → painting, kick → kicked — the child supplies each new word.
plan.note: The child builds, the tutor writes. Fill-blank keeps the root visible so nothing gets changed inside it.
plan.successCriteria: Child builds helping, helped, painting, kicked with the roots unchanged.

script.say: Your turn to help. Take the word help. Grow it an -ing tail… what do we get? Helping! Now an -ed tail… helped! Let's build two more: paint plus -ing… and kick plus -ed. Fill them in — and remember, the root stays exactly as it is.
script.adaptHints: If the child starts changing the root, point at it: 'is help still spelled h-e-l-p in your word?'

wrongAnswers.why: doubled a letter that doesn't need doubling — over-thinking the easy rule
wrongAnswers.remedy: Look at the root: h-e-l-p. For today's easy rule we change NOTHING — write help, then just add the tail.

wrongAnswers.why: mixed up the tails
wrongAnswers.remedy: Which tail did I ask for — -ing or -ed? Look at the tail card and try again.

plan.goal: The lesson's key check: add -ing to play and read it back.
plan.note: Probe after success: 'Did the word play change inside? No — we just added the tail.'
plan.successCriteria: Child spells playing with the root unchanged and reads it back.

script.say: Check time! Add -ing to play — build it, then read your new word back to me out loud.
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'Did the word play change inside? No — we just added the tail.'

blocks.prompt: Read your new word back to me.

check.question: Add -ing to play and read it back.

wrongAnswers.why: changed the root — dropping or adding letters while over-thinking
wrongAnswers.remedy: For this easy rule we change nothing inside the root. Write play — p-l-a-y — then just add -ing. Is play still there in your word?

wrongAnswers.why: mixed up the tails
wrongAnswers.remedy: Which tail did I ask for — -ing or -ed? Point to the -ing tail card and grow that one.

plan.goal: Independent building: add -ing AND -ed to jump, play, help, kick, reading each new word back. Fast finishers: -er/-est on fast.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Watch for altering the root, forgetting to read the new word back, and mixing the tails.
plan.successCriteria: Child adds -ing and -ed to at least three roots with the root unchanged, reading each back.

script.say: Practice time, tail-grower! I'll give you roots and tails — you build the new words and read each one back to me out loud. The golden rule: the root stays exactly as it is. Grow those tails!
script.adaptHints: Frame the actions with the child's life ('you were playing… you jumped…'). Never change the root words themselves.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'The root is changing — but this rule changes nothing.'
Step down: show the root already written; the child only adds the tail.
ONE hint: 'Write the root first, exactly as it is, then the tail.'
Re-ask a smaller version: one suffix only.
Keep it safe: 'Tails are easy — the trick is leaving the root alone.'

plan.goal: Child defines root and suffix and states today's rule; end on process praise.
plan.note: These roots return as 'just-add words' in Lesson 6's warm-up, contrasted with drop-the-e, and again in Lesson 9's sorting office.
plan.successCriteria: Child says: root = main word; suffix = ending/tail; today we just add it on — the root doesn't change.

script.say: Tell me — what's a root, and what's a suffix? And for today's easy words, what do we do to the root? … Exactly: the root is the main word, the suffix is the tail, and we just add it on — the root doesn't change. You grew tails on every word and kept the root word perfectly safe — that's careful spelling.
script.adaptHints: Tease the next lesson: 'Next time, some sneaky words where a letter has to HOP OFF before the tail goes on…' Process praise only.

practiceBank.skill: add a suffix with no spelling change

wrongAnswers.why: spelled the sound instead of the suffix — -ed can sound like /t/
wrongAnswers.remedy: Listen: jumped DOES end with a /t/ sound — but the tail is always spelled -e-d. Write jump, then the -ed tail.

wrongAnswers.why: grabbed the wrong tail
wrongAnswers.remedy: Which tail did I ask for? Check the card: -ed, the 'already happened' tail.

hints: Write the root first, exactly as it is: j-u-m-p.
The 'already happened' tail is always spelled -e-d.

reteach.say: The -ed tail is sneaky — it can SOUND like /t/, but it's always spelled -e-d. Watch: jump + -ed = jumped. Root safe, tail on, spelled e-d no matter how it sounds. Read it back: jumped!

block.prompt: Which is the ROOT word hiding inside 'painting'?
block.explain: Take off the -ing tail and the whole root is left: paint.

wrongAnswers.why: chopped the root too short — took letters off the root as well as the tail
wrongAnswers.remedy: Take off ONLY the tail, -ing. What's left? p-a-i-n-t — paint, the whole root.

wrongAnswers.why: mixed up root and suffix
wrongAnswers.remedy: The root is the MAIN word — the one that makes sense on its own. Can you 'ing'? No! Can you paint? Yes — that's the root.

hints: Take the tail off — what word is left?
The root makes sense all by itself.

reteach.say: Every suffixed word is a root wearing a tail. Painting = paint + -ing. Cover the -ing with your finger… paint! The root is the bit that makes sense on its own. Roots first, tails second — always.

practiceBank.skill: add a suffix with no spelling change

wrongAnswers.why: changed the root — dropped a letter while adding the tail
wrongAnswers.remedy: Check the root: is kick — k-i-c-k — still whole inside your word? Write kick first, THEN grow the tail.

wrongAnswers.why: grabbed the wrong tail
wrongAnswers.remedy: Which tail did I ask for — -ing or -ed? Look at the tail card.

hints: Root first, exactly as it is: k-i-c-k.
Now just add the -ing tail — nothing else changes.

reteach.say: Watch the whole build: kick — k-i-c-k — root safe. Now the tail slides on: -ing. Kicking! Read it back… kicking. The root never lost a single letter. That's the whole rule today.

interestSlots: football or the child's favourite sport for the kick frame

practiceBank.skill: add a suffix with no spelling change

wrongAnswers.why: squashed the tail — lost the e of -ed
wrongAnswers.remedy: The tail is spelled -e-d, both letters. Write paint, then the whole tail: painted.

wrongAnswers.why: grabbed the wrong tail
wrongAnswers.remedy: -ed is the 'already happened' tail. You painted yesterday. Which tail do you need?

hints: The -ed tail keeps both its letters.
paint + e + d — read it back.

reteach.say: Tails come whole — -ed is always BOTH letters, e then d. Paint + -ed = painted. Read it back: painted. If you read your word back every time, missing letters can't hide.

practiceBank.skill: match roots + suffixes to new words

block.prompt: Match each root + tail to the word it builds. Read each one out loud!

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: help+-ed → helped; play+-ing → playing; kick+-ed → kicked; jump+-ing → jumping

wrongAnswers.why: matched the root but ignored which tail
wrongAnswers.remedy: Right root — wrong tail! Look at the ending: -ing or -ed? Match the tail exactly.

wrongAnswers.why: matched by tail only, ignoring the root
wrongAnswers.remedy: Both halves matter: find the word that starts with help AND ends with -ed.

hints: Check the root first, then check the tail.
Read each built word out loud — does it contain the whole root?

reteach.say: Matching is a two-step check: root, then tail. Help + -ed… find the word starting help… ending -ed… helped! Every match keeps the whole root and the whole tail — nothing lost, nothing changed.

block.prompt: Read your four new words back to me — nice and clear!

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: All four words read aloud correctly: jumping, jumped, playing, played

wrongAnswers.why: read the tail as its own syllable
wrongAnswers.remedy: -ed often hides inside the last sound: jumped is ONE beat — jumpt. Say it after me: jumped.

wrongAnswers.answer: reads the roots only, skipping the tails
wrongAnswers.why: eyes stopped at the familiar root
wrongAnswers.remedy: Your eyes know the root — brilliant! Now read right to the end of the tail: jump-ING.

hints: Read all the way to the end of each tail.
-ed sometimes sounds like /t/ — jumped, not jump-ed.

reteach.say: New words deserve a read-back — that's how spellers check their work. Listen: jumping… jumped… playing… played. Hear how -ed sounds different in jumped (/t/) and played (/d/)? Same tail, same spelling, slightly different sound. Now you.

practiceBank.skill: add -er and -est with no spelling change

wrongAnswers.why: doubled a letter that doesn't need doubling
wrongAnswers.remedy: Check the root: f-a-s-t, safe and whole. Just add -er — nothing doubles today.

wrongAnswers.why: grabbed the wrong tail
wrongAnswers.remedy: -er compares two things (faster than you); -est is the champion (the fastest of all). Which did I ask for?

hints: Same easy rule — root stays, tail on.
-er means 'more than' — faster than a snail!

reteach.say: Two new tails, same easy rule! -er compares: I am fast, you are fastER. -est crowns the champion: the fastEST in the world. Fast + -er = faster. Root safe, tail on. Use it out loud: 'I am faster than…' — you finish it!

interestSlots: compare the child's favourite fast animal or vehicle

practiceBank.skill: add -er and -est with no spelling change

wrongAnswers.why: spelled the tail by sound — -est can sound like -ist
wrongAnswers.remedy: The champion tail is always spelled -e-s-t. Write fast, then the whole tail: fastest.

wrongAnswers.why: grabbed the comparing tail instead of the champion tail
wrongAnswers.remedy: -est is the champion of ALL: the fastest. Which tail makes the champion?

hints: Root stays exactly as it is: f-a-s-t.

reteach.say: The -est tail crowns a champion: the fastest, the strongest, the coolest. It's always spelled -e-s-t, even when it mumbles. Fast + -est = fastest. Say a champion sentence: 'The cheetah is the fastest animal!'

block.prompt: A friend writes 'plaing' for play + -ing. What went wrong? Help them fix it.
block.sample: They changed the root — the y fell off. For these easy words nothing inside the root changes: write play, p-l-a-y, then add -ing: playing.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: They changed the root; play must stay whole — play + -ing = playing

wrongAnswers.why: spotted the error but can't name the rule — fragile knowledge
wrongAnswers.remedy: True — but WHAT went wrong? Look for the root inside plaing… can you find p-l-a-y? What's missing?

wrongAnswers.why: shares the change-the-root misconception
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read plaing back… tricky, isn't it? Now find the root: is play still whole in there? Write play first, then the tail.

hints: Hunt for the whole root inside their word — is play all there?
Today's rule: the root never changes.

reteach.say: The best spelling detectives check the root. Plaing — let's hunt for play inside it… p-l-a… the y is GONE! That's what went wrong: the root got changed. Rule: write the root whole — play — then grow the tail: playing. Root safe, tail on, every time.

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level. At level 3, interleave -er/-est items with explain-the-rule items. Include the speak read-back item regularly — new words should be heard, not just built.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach with the root written and visible, then drop one level (root pre-written, child only adds the tail).
adaptivity.masterySignal: Child correctly adds -ing and -ed to at least three roots with the root unchanged, reads each back, and can name root and suffix → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'suffixes with no spelling change'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'The root is changing — but this rule changes nothing.'
Step down: show the root already written; the child only adds the tail.
ONE hint: 'Write the root first, exactly as it is, then the tail.'
Re-ask a smaller version: one suffix only.
Keep it safe: 'Tails are easy — the trick is leaving the root alone.'
adaptivity.personalization: Frame the action words with the child's life — playing their favourite game, kicking a football, painting. The roots and spellings never change.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a build the child nails (drop to -ing on jump if needed) and praise the process: 'you grew tails on every word and kept the root word perfectly safe.'

differentiation.support: Root word pre-written; child only adds the tail and reads it back. Use -ing only first, then -ed.
differentiation.stretch: Add -er and -est to fast (faster, fastest) and use one in a spoken sentence ('I am faster than…').

extension: Find three more just-add roots in a favourite book and grow tails on them.
assessmentEvidence: Child correctly adds -ing and -ed to at least three roots with the root unchanged, and can name root and suffix.
revisitLater: These 'just-add words' open Lesson 6's warm-up, contrasted with drop-the-e (hope → hoping); all four rules meet in Lesson 9's Spelling Sorting Office.
